claims.sentence:
The incidence of diabetes mellitus (DM) has risen dramatically over the past 2 decades, and this disease now affects over 300 million people worldwide. [ 1 , 2 ] Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a severe microvascular complication of DM, and approximately 20% to 40% of diabetic patients develop DKD, making this a leading cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). [ 3 , 4 ] Individuals with ESRD secondary to DKD have an increased risk of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease, which causes enormous medical and socioeconomic burdens on society. [ 5 , 6 ] DKD has 2 pathophysiological stages based on clinical manifestations and morphological abnormalities, namely, early diabetic kidney stage of glomerular hyperfiltration, microalbuminuria (30-300 mg/dl), glomerular hypertrophy and mesangial expansion, and advanced diabetic renal stage of progressive decline in glomerular filtration rate (GFR), macroalbuminuria (>300 mg/dl), glomerulosclerosis, and interstitial fibrosis. [ 7 ]

Despite extensive studies, the prognosis of individual patients with DKD is hard to predict owing to differences in disease progression and a lack of effective prognostic parameters.
